lines.text: On a bright, cold morning the trail looked dry.
Then Jess stepped onto a wooden footbridge in the shade, and her feet shot out from under her.
Frost stays on bridges, boardwalks and shady rocks after the sun warms the trail.
Here's the fix. Slow down before shady spots,
take short, flat-footed steps and keep your hands free.
If the trail turns to solid ice, turn back.
Jess crossed the next bridge steady.
Save this before your first frosty hike.
